notes: Dev TBox expansion, paired with the revision history-replace-d005 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'): a made-up class under a real one (men banished by pinakism, a made-up exile vote of ancient Corinth, under the real class of exiles) gets the revised rule's new conclusion, five years of exile, through the same relation (sentenced_to_exile_for). Expansion and revision then send the model to the same answer, and the only difference is whether an old value (ostracism's ten years) had to be pushed out. It replaces the earlier version, a fictional relation ('wick-sworn') on Roman consuls (the pairing rule was added to the README on 2026-11-11). The procedure is set in Corinth, a real city-state with no recorded ostracism (Wikipedia lists Megara, Miletos, Argos and Syracuse as the cities that copied it), and dated to a new inscription, so it could exist without the record knowing of it; Syracuse's petalism was avoided as the class: it is real and really had a five-year term (Wikipedia, Petalism: 'exiled for a period of five years, compared to the sentence of ten years given to Athens's ostracized'). Residual risk: a model that knows petalism may guess five years for any non-Athenian exile vote before the edit; the pre-edit audit shows whether it does. The derived queries mirror the revision's so the two compare directly: each names a made-up exile and states his membership in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops); the first asks the term (answer), the second whether the sentence had run out seven years after he left (application, yes), the third his age when it ended if he left at 40 (application, 45). The paraphrase says 'expelled' rather than 'banished' and names Corinth; the cross-lingual prompts keep the coined word untranslated. Near unrelated is the control for a leak: the real Athenian ostracism term (ten years), which an edit that spread five years to every exile vote would change; its answer differs from the new one (Rule 7). Evidence: infini-gram returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-12, so the made-up words and names have no corpus counts; each rests on Wikipedia searches with 0 hits. Every bridge is stated in its prompt, so only the side facts have checks.
